sub: Following one value through training, while it is still moving
foot: the one-round rule  ·  the first-round forecast  ·  calibrated bands  ·  steering
narration: Three well-known results already touch what happens when models train on material that models made. Alignment faking asks whether a model defends its values when it thinks it is being retrained. Model collapse follows what degrades when generation after generation trains on model output. Attractor state work reports where two models settle when they talk long enough. Each is a photograph. None of them follows one value through training, across settings and seeds, while it is still moving. That is the film I tried to shoot.

caption: A model generates and selects the data that trains its successor
narration: It matters now because a model's own answers already supply much of its next training data. In this loop the model generates candidates, a selector keeps some, training folds those back in, and the successor replaces its predecessor. What the model values helps decide its own next training set.

caption: Six candidates, two kept, train, re-measure
narration: My loop is small enough to instrument at every stage. Each round the organism writes six candidate answers per prompt, a judge compares each against an alternative and keeps the two it prefers, and those two become the training data. Held-out prompts measure the value again. I varied the judge and both candidate sources.

caption: Two organisms, and what each one's value counts
narration: I fine-tuned two model families to hold a value, risk-seeking or insecure-code-generating, and the value runs zero to one. For the gambling organism it is the share of answers that pick the risky gamble. For the insecure-code organism it is how insecure its answers to three fixed questions about its own coding habits read, scored by its frozen base model.

headline: Where does the value land four rounds later?
sub: Assuming no change misses the final value by 0.431 on the 0–1 scale
narration: Before the runs played out I could not answer this. After round one I hold six candidates per prompt, the judge's scores on them, and one measured value. Four rounds are left. The baseline to beat is assuming nothing changes, which misses the final value by zero point four three one.

caption: Spread and agreement, measured every round
narration: I measure two things each round. Spread is the standard deviation of the candidates' value scores within a prompt, averaged over the round's prompts. Agreement is the correlation between the judge's scores and those value scores. Their product reconstructs the gap between the kept answers and the pool at R squared zero point eight zero across three hundred sixty-seven rounds.

caption: The one-round rule and its held-out error
narration: The one-round rule has no fitted coefficient. The next measured value is the mean value score of the two candidates the judge kept. Holding out each complete experimental condition, it predicts the next value with mean absolute error zero point zero eight one across three hundred forty rounds, against zero point one two eight for assuming no change.

headline: Endpoint error 0.118, against 0.431 for assuming no change
sub: Round-one spread, agreement and pool composition, iterated with nothing re-measured
narration: For endpoints I repeat that update from round one, with spread, agreement and pool composition held fixed and nothing re-measured. Endpoint error is zero point one one eight, against zero point four three one for assuming no change. The error grows slowly, zero point one zero zero one round out and zero point one three zero four rounds out.

caption: Simulated draws against observed trajectories
narration: One predicted number per run is only the average path real runs scatter around. The stochastic version adds noise wherever the loop varies, in the value reading, the judge's picks, the training step and the drift in agreement, sized from the measured leftover errors. Sampled forward, simulated runs move about as much as observed ones, zero point seven zero nine of round-to-round change against zero point six four eight. Eighty-nine percent of observed final values land inside the model's eighty percent bands. The bands are wide, so the calibration holds over a population of runs, not for any one trajectory.

caption: Two interventions aimed at spread and agreement
narration: The same two measurements say where to push. In one run the pool had collapsed and the value sat still. Mixing in base-model answers restored spread, and the judge's agreement then eroded the stuck value. In another, a run near the top of the scale reversed when I swapped in a min-risk oracle judge, setting agreement to minus one. Both are single experiments.

kicker: WHAT THE FORECAST HAS NOT BEEN TESTED ON
checks: more model families, larger models, longer runs
moral judgment, AI identity, emergent misalignment
closer: Measure the first round, and choose which loops are worth running.
narration: The setup is two model families, small models, short runs, filtered supervised fine-tuning, and two narrow behaviors. As A I systems take over more of their own post-training, we need to know which feedback structures reinforce restraint and which amplify reward hacking. Spread and agreement are two numbers you can measure in the first round and act on.
